subject: Any suggestions for adding resource use together?

messages.author: 7840f0c79a42cce9
messages.subject: Any suggestions for adding resource use together?
parts:
I have a bad cold and am struggling with this so hoped someone else might have an idea.

I have my virtual hospital in simmer with wards as resources. I have the get_mon_resources output from a number of replications, with timestamps and the ward population at that point (as "server").

 If I want to graph the total of two wards eg "A" plus "B" I'm struggling. I can use round_date to get the timepoints rounded to the nearest day, but can't guarantee there will be a "server" row for either ward during that period (eg if it was very quiet). I also struggle to cope with multiple replications.

 I've tried using xts for timeseries data which works well for a single replication but there doesn't seem to be an obvious way to work with many replications:

combine_resources_to_xts<-function(data,resources) {
  xts<-xts()
  for (res in resources) {
    print(res)
    tmp2<-filter(data,resource==res)
    print(nrow(tmp2))
    xts2<-to.period(xts(x=tmp2$server,order.by=tmp2$rtime),"days")
    if (length(xts)>0) {
      xts_union<-na.locf(merge(xts,index(xts2)))
      xts2_union<-na.locf(merge(xts2,index(xts)))
      xts<-xts_union+xts2_union
    } else {
      xts<-xts2
    }
  }
  names(xts)<-c("Open","High","Low","Close")
  return(xts)
}

Where data is the output of get_mon_resources with data$rtime<-round_date(data$time,unit="day")

Has anyone else tried to add two resources together when analysing the output of simmer runs? Grateful for any thoughts.

tom

messages.author: 7840f0c79a42cce9
messages.subject: Re: Any suggestions for adding resource use together?
parts:
Had an idea which seems to work using dplyr:

eg to combine resources "ICU" and "AMU1":

test<-resources %>%
  filter(str_detect(resource,"(ICU|AMU1)")) %>%
  group_by(replication,resource) %>%
  complete(rtime=seq(min(rtime),max(rtime),by="day")) %>%
  group_by(replication,resource,rtime) %>%
  summarize(mean(server)) %>%
  fill("mean(server)") %>%
  group_by(replication,rtime) %>%
  summarize(sum(`mean(server)`))

Just in case anyone else ever has this issue!

tom

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Re: Any suggestions for adding resource use together?
parts:
Great, thanks for sharing! Try this one (not tested):

resources %>%
group_by(resource, replication) %>%
mutate(server = diff(c(0, server))) %>%
ungroup() %>%
mutate(resource = ifelse(grepl("ICU|AMU1", resource), "ICU+AMU1",
resource)) %>%
group_by(resource, replication) %>%
mutate(server = cumsum(server))

Iñaki

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Re: Any suggestions for adding resource use together?
parts:
Thanks - this is exactly what I was trying to do - it's a much better solution than my own as it doesn't involve recreating all the times, and can be arbitrarily extended to add other groupings. The only residual advantage of mine is that you end up with a regular time series as a side-effect, which may be easier to play with later.

tom
